messages.author: 2e9423a4b20e1401
messages.subject: Model parses but doesn't compile
parts:
Hi guys,

Stan is looking great; nice work!

There's an issue I hope you can help me with. The original for-loop version of my code was taking overnight to get just a few samples, so I made some changes to vectorize things. This ran MUCH faster (about 20 minutes for 1000 samples). But I'm finding it to be very fragile. I've attached a version that uses a common standard deviation across several variables - this parses fine, but fails to compile.

I've never done template programming in C++, so the output is tricky for me to follow. Any advice for connecting errors like this to problems in the original file?

I'm using g++ (Ubuntu/Linaro 4.7.3-1ubuntu1) 4.7.3

Thanks!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Model parses but doesn't compile
parts:
Thanks for the detailed report. It's definitely a bug
on our side. The behavior should be that anything that can
be translated by stanc should be compilable by g++ and clang++.

We're in the middle of changing how much of this works, but
your model's still problematic on our develop branch. The problem
we get is in the optimizer instantiations.

I'll take a look and get back to you.

As to the speed, one issue you may be having is with the
odd prior for deviation parameters asig and bsig:

parameters {
...
real<lower=0> asig;
real<lower=0> bsig;
...
model {
...
lp__ <- lp__ - log(asig) - log(bsig);
...

This is an improper prior taking on the linear scale (where
propto is multiplicative):

p(asig) propto 1/asig

so that on the log scale (where propto is additive)

log p(asig) propto -log(asig)

Is there a motivation for this prior? And what happens to the
asig and bsig variables in terms of mixing and values?

- Bob

P.S. The error novel output's tricky even for those of us with
a couple of years of experience with C++ templates :-) It's
often useful to use both g++ and clang++ as their error reporting
is quite different.

This is an improper scale-invariant prior. I usually use it as a starting point in cases like this. I like the scale-invariant interpretation, and it's computationally very nice. You have to watch out to be sure the posterior is proper, of course.

I can't tell you what happens here, since I can't run it :)

But in general, I either see relatively nice behavior (in which case I don't mess with it), or the log is uniform over the range of floating points (in which case I need to give an informative prior or make other changes in the model).

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Model parses but doesn't compile
parts:
That was easy to track down. The problem is that
we forgot to declare "add" as a reserved word and
it's conflicting with the built-in function add(),
which we use for polymorphic addition (scalar + matrix, etc.)

If you rename your variable "add" you should be good to go.

We'll add it to the list of reserved words or qualify the calls
so that either the model you have will work, or you will get
a reasonable error message indicating that "add" is reserved.
I just filed an issue if you'd like to track our progress fixing:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/193

It will be fixed before 2.0 is out.

- Bob
